newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africans seek amnesty over Biko death --sources.
newsitem.headline: S.Africans seek amnesty over Biko death --sources.

text.p: People involved in the 1977 death of Steve Biko, one of South Africa's most celebrated anti-apartheid activists, have applied for amnesty to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, a commission source said on Tuesday.
Police beat Biko during interrogation and he died still in custody. The officers involved told an inquest that Biko had fallen and hit his head, but anti-apartheid activists accused them of murder.

"Amnesty forms have been lodged concerning Biko's death," the source told reporters called to a commission news conference in the town where Biko was detained. "All we've got so far is the forms. Full disclosure will come later."

Lawyer Francois van der Merwe said he would attend the news conference in Port Elizabeth later on Tuesday with members of the truth commission, where more details were expected to be given of the amnesty applications.
"I represent say 10 to 20 people involved in various events...yes, including the Biko incident," van der Merwe said, adding that his clients included former and serving police officers.

Biko's death in Pretoria after a month in police detention was one of the most notorious incidents in apartheid South Africa and hardened foreign opposition to the system of forced racial segregation. He became a martyr for anti-apartheid activists at home and overseas.
